text: {"question":"How does each model treat the Hubble constant when relating the dimensionless Hubble parameter to observational data, and what additional parameters are introduced to replace the standard cosmological parameters in each case?","reference_answer":"In the first model, the Hubble constant H₀ is used to define the dimensionless Hubble parameter E=H/H₀ and the new free parameters page and η replace the standard α₁ and α₂, allowing the redshift–time relation to be solved. In the second model, H₀ is still the baseline Hubble constant, but the interaction rate amplitude ξᵢₑₙ is introduced as the sole extra parameter beyond ΛCDM, with the DE equation‑of‑state fixed at wide=−0.999 to avoid instability."}
